# Drafting procedures for an AI assistant

RegRem Engine checks the proof and an AI assistant the financial institution allows drafts it. These pages are the written procedure for each drafting job, one page a job, written for any assistant and naming none. Give the assistant the page and the finding folder, then run the check on what it wrote. Commands run from the kit root, and `finding` stands for `finding/finding`, or `py -I finding\finding.py` on Windows.

| Job | Page | What it writes | What it has to pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Turn the letter into a plan | [draft-plan.md](draft-plan.md) | plan.md | `finding check` prints no "Not ready" line |
| Describe each evidence file | [draft-covers.md](draft-covers.md) | the What and For lines of each cover | `finding check` counts every file |
| Draft the closure memo | [draft-memo.md](draft-memo.md) | closure/memo.md | every row on the list gets a person's ruling or a fix |
| Propose a ruling for each row | [propose-rulings.md](propose-rulings.md) | closure/proposed-rulings.md | a person copies the ones they accept |
| Answer internal audit's questions | [answer-audit.md](answer-audit.md) | a draft answer outside the record | each answer cites the folder |

## The rules for every job

1. The assistant drafts, and a person decides. It never types a Signed by, Produced by, Approved by, Never signed or Status line, never writes closure/rulings.md or closure/record.md, and never runs `finding sign`.
2. It works only inside the finding folder, on a machine and a service the institution has approved for that information. If the institution allows no assistant for a supervisory finding, a person does these jobs by hand, and the check works the same.
3. It copies nothing from the finding folder to anywhere outside it.
4. Every figure, date and quotation it writes carries a cite to the page it came from, in digits and full dates so the check can read it. A claim it cannot cite goes in as a question for a person.
5. The check reads what it wrote and gives the same answer every run. Run `finding check` after every job. Until a person signs the covers, each draft cover is one row saying how many claims match its pages, so read the other rows as the test of the draft: a claim that does not match keeps its own row, and the assistant fixes it or asks. Once the covers are signed, the whole list is the test. Run `finding eval` when the memo is ready, because it plants errors in the claims that match a draft's pages too. A wrong figure that sits on the cited page still ties, so a person reads each sentence against its page.

## How these pages improve

A miss a reviewer catches can become two things. One is a change to the procedure page, written in general terms. The other is an invented case in [library/cases](../library/README.md), which every later release has to pass. Neither carries anything from an institution's folder, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) says how to propose one.

# Draft the closure memo

Goal: write closure/memo.md, saying what was done, by whom and when, with a cite after every figure, date and quotation.

Reads: plan.md, the covers and the documents, each to its last page, because a later page may amend an earlier one. Reads the page before citing it.

Writes: closure/memo.md, one block per milestone, each opening with the milestone's id, with one sentence a line. The check counts a paragraph as one line, so every row on a long paragraph names the same line. With one sentence a line, a row on the list points at one sentence. This example ties in finding/cases/IA-CMP-02:

```text
M1, acknowledgement letters.
Since 2026-05-04 the complaint system sends the acknowledgement letter on the business day after a complaint is logged [EV-21 p1].
The Head of Complaints signed the procedure and sample on 2026-05-28 [EV-21 p2].

Tested control: M1, the acknowledgement letter procedure
Fix effective: 2026-05-04 [EV-21 p1]
Sample period: 2026-05-04 to 2026-05-22 [EV-21 p2]
```

## Rules

- Put a cite such as `[EV-07 p2]` straight after every figure, date and quotation. Its id is the last word of the file's For line. A PDF page is its printed page. A Word, CSV, email or text file is always p1, so the cite does not say where in the file a figure sits. A workbook page is a visible sheet, in workbook order, and hidden sheets, rows and columns do not count. An Excel percent or date reads as its stored fraction or serial number, so it goes on the list for a person.
- Write each cite exactly as `[EV-07 p2]`. A cite answers only for the sentence it sits in, even when a line wraps, so give every sentence that holds a claim its own cite. The page names a cite written another way, such as `[EV-07, p2]`, and reads it as no cite.
- Copy figures character for character from the cited page. Quote exactly, with straight double quotes, and quote two words or more. The check also reads a quotation in single quotes, straight or curly, when it holds three words or more. A quotation with a bracketed insertion or an ellipsis goes on the list for a person, so quote whole words where you can.
- Write every figure in digits and every date in full, as YYYY-MM-DD. The check reads no figure written in words, and no bare year, ordinal, month with no year, quarter label such as Q3, fiscal year such as FY26 or date with a two-digit year, so a claim written that way goes unchecked. A four-digit number from 1900 to 2099 reads as a year, so write a count such as 2,020 with its comma. A quarter with its year after it, such as Q3 2026 or 3Q 2026, is read as that quarter, and Excel's Aug-26 as August 2026. A number straight after version, v or Rev., such as version 3.1, is a label and needs no cite. The page names figures in words, years and two-digit-year dates on its `Not checked:` lines and leaves the rest to a reader.
- The claim count on the page is every date and quotation the check reads, and every number in digits that stands apart from letters. So a figure inside a quotation counts as well as the quotation, and so does the 6 in action 6. A number is joined to letters when a letter stands straight before it, or a letter and then a dash, slash or colon. Such a number is no claim, as in E11471, L2, S-07 or CHG-2026-04471. Other ids hold claims, so the 0173 in QA26Q2-0173, both numbers in 12345-6, the 11471 in ID 11471 and the 4471 in #4471 each count. A version number, a clock time, a list number in order and the forms the rule above says the check does not read are no claim. Nor is a section number or a part label such as Part 3 in a heading, as [finding/README.md](../finding/README.md#check) describes, though Part 3 in a sentence counts.
- Use one sentence per claim where you can, and start each sentence on a line of its own, so a row on the list points at one thing.
- Where a page holds two figures of one kind, such as two counts or two dates, quote the whole labelled line, so a figure moved to the other's place goes on the list.
- For each control internal audit will test, add a Tested control block with the date the fix took effect and the sample period, and cite each date to the page that holds it. Fix effective is the date the fix starts to bind, which can fall after the date it was approved or published. A date with no cite goes on the list, and so does a sample that starts before the fix. Nothing else goes in the block: the next line is read as ordinary memo text.
- Say what is unfinished, in plain words. Never say the finding is closed, because only the issuer closes a finding. Until the issuer's entry is in the record, such a line is a row on the list that stops the signature, and no ruling clears it, so it has to be reworded. Any other use of the word closed, such as accounts closed in error, goes on the list for the owner to rule on, so use it only where the evidence does. A use in the letter's own words, such as alerts closed without escalation copied from a required action, is no row.
- Leave signature state to the screen, and write what the documents show. A sentence such as "no cover is signed" turns false once a person signs.
- Write no reason why a row should be cleared into the memo. That is the next job.

## Passing

`finding check` prints the list. Until the covers are signed, a clean draft leaves one row for each draft cover, which waits on a person's signature, and rows a person has to decide. A claim that does not match its page keeps its own row, so fix it before handing over. Then run `finding eval <folder>`, which plants errors in memory and shows what the check would catch and what a person still has to read for. A figure in the right sentence that is wrong but sits on the cited page ties, so a reviewer reads each sentence against its page.

# Finding MRA-CMP-07
Identifier: MRA-CMP-07
Institution: Wrenfield Example Bank
Issuer: the Supervisor
Letter date: 2026-01-15
Kind of matter: supervisory finding
Owner role: Head of Complaints

## Concern

The bank does not classify customer complaints consistently. In the second half of 2025, complaints that asked for a fee reversal were often logged as service issues. Those complaints missed the fee-review queue and were left out of the fee lines in complaint trend reports to the board.

## Cause

The complaint taxonomy had no category for fee disputes. The intake procedure gave staff no rule for a complaint that mentions a fee, so each handler chose a category. No one reviewed the quality of complaint classification after intake.

## Consequence

The board and senior management received complaint trend reports that understated fee complaints. Customers with valid fee disputes waited longer for an answer, and some may not have received a refund they were owed.

## Corrective action

The bank must revise the complaint taxonomy to cover fee disputes, reissue the intake procedure with a rule for fee complaints and train intake staff on it, test classification quality on the complaints it reclassifies, and extend the taxonomy to every channel through which customers complain.

## Commitment

The bank must send the Supervisor a written remediation plan approved by its board within 30 days of this letter, with an owner role and a committed date for each action. The Supervisor will consider the matter for closure only after internal audit has tested the remediation.

# finding: one folder per finding

When your financial institution tells the board and the Supervisor that a finding is fixed, code has checked every figure and date written in digits, every quotation and every document in the closure package against its evidence. Whatever did not check sits on a one-page list with a role against it. The finding owner signs, internal audit tests the fix, the issuer closes, internal audit for its own findings and the Supervisor for its own, and nothing about the finding leaves the institution.

Everything in `cases/` is invented.

## The folder

```
MRA-CMP-07/
  finding.md           the Supervisor's letter
  plan.md              one row per milestone
  evidence/            one file per piece
  closure/memo.md      the closure memo
  closure/rulings.md   rulings on the list
  closure/record.md    board approval, signature, closers
  closure/measures.md  hours booked, and what internal audit sent back
  closure/finding-log.jsonl   one line for each corrected paste or restarted record
  .finding-state.json  hashes, deny list, signature
```

Copy a folder with `cp -R folder copy`. `cp -R folder/* copy` drops the dot file, and with it the record of signed files.

`new` takes a path whose last part is the finding's id, makes the folder there and writes the templates, with no SYNTHETIC line to delete. It refuses a path inside the kit's own folders, so an institution's finding never lands in the kit. An evidence file opens with four lines:

```
What: EV-07 Complaint intake procedure
For: M2 EV-07
Signed by: Head of Complaints, 2026-03-14
Status: FINAL
```

The lines may sit in any order, together at the top of the file, and a blank line ends them. `Revised: YYYY-MM-DD` records a later change, `Source:` says where the text came from, and `Checked by:` names a second person who compared a typed page. `finding covers` also writes a Source line and a comment.

Signed by is one of four signature lines, and a person types the one that fits the file:

- `Signed by: Head of Complaints, 2026-03-14` for a document a person signs, such as a procedure, minutes, an attestation or a report a person issues.
- `Produced by: case manager aging report, 2026-04-30` for system output, such as an MI workbook or a data extract, on the as-at date a person confirmed.
- `Approved by: EV-29` for a document the institution approved by a separate record, such as a method approved by email, naming that record's evidence id.
- `Never signed: training deck` for material an institution never signs, such as a quick reference card. Its ties count, and it never counts toward a milestone.

System output, such as a monthly MI workbook, a system aging report or a data extract, comes from a system as at a date. Its cover gives that system or report and the as-at date a person confirmed, in place of the Signed by line:

```
Produced by: case manager aging report, 2026-04-30
```

An institution often approves a document by a separate record, such as a QA method approved by email, a lookback method approved on a signed sheet or an MI pack accepted in a resolved minute. The document's cover then names that record's evidence id in place of the Signed by line, and the record gets its own cover, signed by the role that approved:

```
Approved by: EV-29
```

The document counts as signed on the record's date once the record is present and signed by a person. A record that is missing, unsigned or changed leaves the document unsigned with that reason, as in `EV-26 is approved by EV-29, which is missing.` So does a Revised line dated after the approval. A record that is system output, never signed or approved in its turn by another record carries no signature, so it approves nothing.

Training decks, quick reference cards, board MI packs, file copies of letters and most emails carry no signature by nature. The cover of such a file says so with a few words of what it is, in place of the Signed by line, and its Status is FINAL:

```
Never signed: training deck
```

Its ties count, and it puts no draft row on the list. It never counts toward a milestone, so listed beside signed files it neither signs the milestone nor holds it up. A milestone that lists only such files stays unsigned, with a reason that asks for the file that shows the milestone done.

A Signed by line that names a role wins over a Produced by, Approved by or Never signed line in the same cover, so a document someone should sign still needs its signature.

plan.md holds one row per milestone, and its Evidence cell lists every file that shows the milestone done. List the file that completes it, such as a lookback's final report, before that file exists, under an evidence id kept for it, such as EV-61. The check keeps the milestone unsigned while that file is missing, as in `Present, unsigned: EV-61 is missing.`, so a lookback two-thirds done never reads as signed on its methodology and approval alone. Mark the file that completes the milestone with `(done)` after its id, as in `EV-27, EV-28 (done)`, and reserve the id with its mark before the file exists. The milestone's date, and so its lateness, is then that file's signature or as-at date, and every other file the row lists still has to be present and signed, apart from a file never signed. A row with no mark keeps the newest date among its files. A row with two marks stops the check, which names its line.

The board's approval of the plan is an evidence file too, holding the minutes. Its `For:` line ends `E-PLAN-1`, as in `For: PLAN E-PLAN-1`, and it is FINAL and signed by the role that keeps the minutes, such as `Signed by: Company Secretary, 2026-02-10`. No milestone lists it. Until it counts as signed, every committed date reads `proposed`, the page asks the board for its approval of the plan and sign refuses. When the minutes are there and do not count, the Plan approval line gives the reason, such as `E-PLAN-1 changed since it was signed`. Once they count, the committed dates freeze. A date changed in plan.md afterwards shows as moved, lateness counts from the approved date, and the board is asked to approve the change. An added milestone asks the same, and neither stops the signature. A milestone taken out of plan.md afterwards does stop the signature, and sign gives the reason. Minutes signed again with a later date approve the plan as it then stands. The page keeps the date the board first approved beside each date it moved. The board summary flags a move only when the approval that first carried the new date came after the old date had passed, and the flag stays after later approvals.

Evidence arrives under the institution's own file names. Copy each file into evidence/, start its name with its evidence id and keep the institution's file name after the id, as in `EV-07 TM Alert Backlog MI - Mar 2026 v2 FINAL.xlsx`, then run `finding covers`. A milestone signed after its committed date is flagged on the board summary with how many days late, counted from the date of the file plan.md marks done, as in `Present on 2026-05-15, the date of EV-28, which plan.md marks done.` With no mark it counts from the newest signature or as-at date among the files, so a routine re-signature flags too. The quarterly progress starts at the quarter of the first committed date. Two evidence files with the same bytes, such as a scan saved under a second name, are named for the team under Needs a person, and `finding covers` names them too. Sign goes ahead with them. Any other use of the word closed, such as accounts closed in error, goes on the list the same way for the owner to rule on. A use is no row when the two words before closed and the two after it stand in that order in finding.md, as when the plan copies the letter's alerts closed without escalation. A line that says the finding itself is closed stays a row all the same. Every such row stays off the list once the closer's record exists. A wrong paste of the letter is corrected with `finding/finding check <folder> --repaste`, which keeps the evidence record, the deny list and the signature, and says so on every later page and in the log.

Each entry in closure/record.md, internal audit's, a closer's or the board's, counts once its reference, date and role each have a real form. A placeholder such as TBD, to follow or XXX counts for nothing, and so do a value under three characters, a reference with no digit and a date after the check. An entry dated before the first check counts, and its line says the check cannot see when it was made. A role is taken as written, such as Company Secretary or Head of Regulatory Relations. A name typed there prints as written, unless it is on the deny list, which stops the page.

In the memo, a cite such as `[EV-12 p2]` names page 2 of the file whose `For:` line ends `EV-12`. A heading such as `## Page 2` starts a page, and a file without one is one page. The kit's tie-out engine reads the cited page for each figure, date and quotation. A cite answers for its own sentence, even across a wrapped line, and a list item after a bullet or a list number is a sentence of its own. A quotation is read in double quote marks, or in single marks when it holds three words or more, and one with a bracketed insertion or an ellipsis goes on the list for a person. A cite written another way, such as `[EV-12, p2]`, `[ EV-12 p2 ]`, `[EV-12 pp. 1-2]` or `[EV-12 p2, EV-13 p1]`, is no cite, its page numbers are no claims, and its row names the form the check reads. A claim that does not tie goes on the list, as does a missing cite or one to a missing file, or to a file no milestone lists that is not signed. A draft cover has one row for the claims that match its pages and they count as no ties, and a claim that does not match keeps its own row. A heading's figures count, a number that opens it included, except a section number and a number that labels a part, such as Part 3 or Appendix 1. A number straight after version, v or Rev., such as version 3.1, v2 or Rev. 4, is a label anywhere in the memo, and no claim. A section number is written as `2.`, `2)`, `(2)`, `2:` or `2 -`, or as `2.1` before a capitalised word, or is `1` or the number after the last heading's, as `## 3 Findings` after `## 2 Method`. A list number is no figure when it is 1 or the next in its list, so a figure such as `(12)` opening a line counts. So do the dates on a `Fix effective:` or `Sample period:` line. A sample period that starts before its control's `Fix effective:` date is a row too, which sits on the list without being one of the claims. A figure written in words, a number read as a year and a date with a two-digit year, such as 1-Jul-26, are no claims, and the page names each on a `Not checked:` line. A date ties at the precision written. A month or a quarter ties a page that shows the same period or a date inside it, however many such dates the page holds. The figures in its sentence are checked as before. On an evidence page, a day, month and year split by one line break read as one date, unless a figure stands before the day, as in a table row or Page 1 of 3, or a label such as Table 3, Page 2 or Section 4 does. Excel's Aug-26 and Aug-2026 read as August 2026, in the memo and on a page. On the page of a saved email with a Date line, a day and month with no year take the year that puts them nearest that date. So 29 January in an email dated 21 Oct 2026 reads as 2027-01-29. Anywhere else such a date is not read. The time and zone on an email's Date line, such as 20:05:33 +0000, are no figures, and its date still reads as a date. A page the memo cites that has no text and nothing typed is named on the page, and a page it does not cite is not. The tool never changes the memo.

A row leaves the list when a line in closure/rulings.md clears it with the owner role, a date no later than the check and a reason, and the page prints each cleared row. A ruling clears one row. The second cell is what the row prints after "To rule, name:", the claim and a short mark for its cite and sentence, so a ruling cannot clear a different claim:

```
Line 8 | March 2026 #f2ba27f8 | cleared | Head of Complaints | 2026-11-04 | The page says January to March.
```

If the memo moves, a cleared ruling follows its claim to the new line while the memo holds that claim, cite and sentence once. Change the sentence or the cite and the row returns to the list under a new mark. The page then says the old ruling names no row and gives the row that prints its claim, as in `Ruling at rulings.md line 5 names no row: the row on line 8 prints EV-12 draft #30243f6b.` The owner rules again under the new mark. A ruling dated before its cited file was signed again stops counting, and the page says why. A ruling of `fix the memo` or `fix the evidence` gets the same line while a row prints its claim under another mark. Once no row does, it stays in the file without a word.

## Sign

`sign` runs only at a terminal, which stops a script by accident and proves nobody's identity. The institution's access controls supply that. A real finding is signed on the machine's date. `--today` works on sign only while the first line of finding.md is a shipped case's SYNTHETIC line, word for word. `finding new` writes no SYNTHETIC line, and on any other first line `sign` refuses `--today` with "drop --today". A typed date shows on the page and in record.md beside the machine's own date. It refuses while a row is on the list, the memo is empty, a tie rests on a page typed into a cover with no Checked by line, or with one dated before the check that first saw that page change, a milestone is below signed, the plan is still proposed, a milestone was taken out of plan.md after the board approved the plan, a file is not counted, record.md lacks the board's reference, date or role, a signed file sits under another id, or a file came in under the id of a signed file that went before it came in. The signer types the owner role, then the first eight characters of a fingerprint over the memo, rulings, letter, plan, evidence, board approval and the tool's own code, including the engine and the document reader. The signature and the kit's release go into record.md. A later change to a covered file asks for a fresh signature. Entries the closers make in record.md do not, because they come after the signature: internal audit's, the Supervisor's and the issue-management owner's. When internal audit enters at least eight characters on `Internal audit tested fingerprint:`, the page compares them with the folder as it stands and asks for a fresh test if the folder moves on.

## The log

closure/finding-log.jsonl gets one line when `check --repaste` records a corrected paste of the letter, and the first such correction starts the file. After a lost state file, the next check adds a `record restarted` line only when closure/finding-log.jsonl is already there, and before then it writes no line. Every log line names the kind, the issuer and the first check.

## Measures

closure/measures.md holds what the Measures line on the check page counts, and no signature covers it. One line a month for hours and one line for each thing internal audit sends back:

```
Hours | 2026-10 | 38
Hours | 2026-11 | 12.5
Sent back | 2026-11-02 | Line 8 | the figure was the draft's | missed by the check
```

Part hours count, and so does the same line written as a table row. The check adds hours exactly and prints the total as it stands, such as 50.5 hours. A line that starts with Hours or Sent back and cannot be read, such as `Hours | 2026-11 | 1,240` or `Hours: 38`, is named on the page for the engagement team and counts for nothing.

## Fitting it to a financial institution

Two optional lists sit beside finding.md, or one folder up for the whole engagement. `denylist.txt` holds terms that must never print, one a line, matched in any letter case and with or without accents. `role-words.txt` holds ordinary words or phrases never to treat as a name, and a line there clears a term the check took for a name, even after a refused run. `denylist.txt` wins over it. A run of capitalised words that holds a document word, such as Procedure, Policy, Report, Plan, Minutes, Register or Methodology, is a title, so the check never takes it for a name, and the institution's file names can keep it. Every refusal over a term the check took from the letter offers role-words.txt, the refusal over a file name included, because renaming one of the institution's files breaks its link to the institution's records. A line can also clear one word of the institution's name, such as First in First Fenmoor Trust Bank, on the pages, and that word then passes in every form. The institution's full name never clears, so its refusal never offers the file. The check page prints only counts, as `Deny list: 3 names.`, and adds `; role-words.txt cleared 1 word of the institution's name.` when a line did. `finding/finding check <folder> --names` prints the names, for the person who asks.

The hours `finding size` assumes sit in a third optional file, `size-assumptions.txt`, in the same two places. It holds one line for each assumption the team has timed, and a line left out keeps the kit's value. A line beside the finding wins over the one in the folder above. The file changes no fingerprint, and `size` says how many lines it read. A folder of findings reads the file in that folder, and a finding's own file still wins for that finding, with its values named on the run's closing line. These are the kit's values:

```
minutes a claim by hand: 10
memo versions: 3
hours a status report: 2
minutes to find a signed file: 30
hours a rework round: 8
minutes a cover: 10
minutes a ruling: 15
minutes to read a claim: 10
rework rounds with the kit: 1
minutes a status report with the kit: 15
minutes to type and compare a page: 15
```

The templates, the plan columns and the record fields are constants at the top of finding.py. A column the institution adds to plan.md is read past wherever it sits, so it needs no change there. Renaming a column or a record field the check reads, or adding a kind of matter, needs a code change and a self-test case. A change to finding.py changes every fingerprint, and `python3 -I finding/release.py` refreshes RELEASE.json. With no version named it steps the kit to a site version, such as 0.7.1+site.1, so a kit changed at an institution never reads as the published release.

## Known limits

Each of these is open in 0.7.1 and can turn up in ordinary material, so a person reads for it.

- A person's name inside a title, such as the Natarajan Report, stays off the deny list, because a run holding a document word is a title. Put such a name in denylist.txt.
- An uncited claim in a lettered list such as a) or i), a middle-dot bullet or a table row borrows the cite on the next line, so it can tie.
- June of 2026 and the typo May. 22, 2026 are not read as dates, so a wrong one can pass.
- A month or a quarter ties any date inside it on its page. So a wrong month the page also shows, as in a monthly table, ties, as a wrong figure the page holds elsewhere does.
- A bracketed id such as (CP-07) reads as a misspelt cite, so the sentence's real cite is lost and its row asks for [CP-07].
- A cite written [EV-21 pp. 1, 2] or [EV-21 pages 1 and 2] gives each page number a row, and a cite after the point, as in (See [EV-21 p2].), or a point in i.e. leaves a claim with no cite.

- In closure/record.md a reference such as IA-2026-TBC counts, while a two-letter role such as IA and a reference with no digit, such as BRC minutes (July), count for nothing.
- A person's name typed in a record role line prints as written unless it is on the deny list.

## Reference

A check exits 0 when nothing needs a person, 1 otherwise, and 2 on a usage error. An unsigned folder still needs its owner, so it exits 1. `--today YYYY-MM-DD` checks as of another date, and works on sign only as the Sign section says. `--names` and `--repaste` are the two options above. `python3 -I finding/selftest.py` tests the tool, including that the kit's own files import only modules on a fixed list and start no process.

# The finding owner

This page is for the person on the business side who owns a finding, such as the Head of Complaints in the invented case MRA-CMP-07. The tool asks two things of you. You rule on each row the check could not tie, and once nothing is left you sign.

The check is plain code with no AI model in it, so one folder checked as of one date always prints the same page. It looks for each figure, date and quotation in the closure memo on the evidence page its cite names. Whether the fix works is left to you, internal audit and the issuer.

## The page you read

From the root folder of the repository:

```sh
python3 -I finding/finding.py check finding/cases/MRA-CMP-07 --today 2026-11-04
```

The `--today` option fixes the date so your screen matches this one, trimmed where it shows `...`:

```text
Finding MRA-CMP-07, a supervisory finding from the Supervisor dated 2026-01-15. Owner: Head of Complaints. Checked as of 2026-11-04, kit release 0.7.1.
...
Memo check: 13 claims, 7 tie, 3 on the list, 1 cleared.
  Line 8: 1,248 is cited to EV-07 p2, and the page does not hold it; the nearest figures on the page are 1,284 and 2. To rule, name: 1,248 #972adb19
  Line 10: EV-12, which is a draft, holds 4 claims, on lines 10, 15 and 16, that match its pages and wait on a person's signature. To rule, name: EV-12 draft #81b3b231
  Line 16: the sample period for M2 starts 2026-01-05, before the fix took effect on 2026-03-17, so the sample mixes items from before and after the fix. To rule, name: sample period for M2 #106ddd50
  Cleared: line 8, March 2026, by the Head of Complaints on 2026-11-04: The page says January to March, and the plan year is 2026.
  7 ties rest on text a person typed: 7 in plain-text evidence, none on a page typed into a cover.
  Not checked: 1 figure written in words, line 6 (three).
Signature: none yet.
...
Needs a person:
  Head of Complaints: M2, the list (3 rows).
...
```

The Owner field names the role your rulings and signature must carry. The command exits 1 while anyone still has something to do.

## What each row means

Each row opens with the memo line it concerns, and a row you can rule on ends with the words a ruling uses to name it.

- Line 8 says 1,248 and the cited page says 1,284, which looks like two digits swapped in typing. The memo is wrong.
- Line 10 is one row for a draft. The quality review EV-12 supports four claims in the memo, and they wait until someone signs it.
- Line 16 says the tested sample starts before the fix took effect, so it mixes items from both sides of the fix.

Other rows name a missing cite, a cite to a file that is not there, or a page with no text that someone has to type. No ruling clears a row for a memo or plan that calls the finding closed before the closer has recorded it, so someone rewords the line.

Below the rows, each Cleared line gives the role, date and reason of a past ruling. The Not checked line names figures the check skipped, such as a number written in words.

## How to rule

A ruling is one line in closure/rulings.md. It gives the memo line, the name the row prints at its end, the ruling, your role, a date and a reason.

```text
Line 16 | sample period for M2 #106ddd50 | cleared | Head of Complaints | 2026-11-04 | Items from before 2026-03-17 were drawn on purpose as a baseline error rate.
```

A `cleared` ruling takes the row off the list and prints your reason on every later page. To send a row back, rule `fix the memo`, or `fix the evidence` when a document must change or be signed again. That row stays on the list until the fix lands, and your line stays as a record that the check caught it.

The check ignores a ruling from another role, one dated after the check or one with no reason, and says why under the rows. The mark after `#` stands for the claim, its cite and its sentence. Reword the sentence or move the cite and the row returns under a new mark, so you rule again.

The tool accepts `cleared` on any row that offers a name, a wrong figure included, so the restraint is yours. Use it only when you can see the memo is right and why the check missed it, such as a figure the page spells out in words. Send a wrong figure back every time. A colleague or an AI assistant may draft rulings for you to accept. The check cannot tell who typed a line, so every line naming your role counts as yours.

## The fingerprint and the signature

Sign refuses while a row is on the list, a milestone is unsigned or the board has not approved the plan, among other reasons. When no refusal is left, sign shows the full check page first and then asks two questions. Here it runs on a copy of the second invented case:

```sh
cp -R finding/cases/IA-CMP-02 walk-02
python3 -I finding/finding.py sign walk-02 --today 2026-11-04
```

```text
Ready to sign: the folder's fingerprint is e8196695. Internal audit records this as what it tests.

Type the finding owner's role to sign: Head of Complaints
Fingerprint e8196695310808ca7b781c85652770d0806694a69b43af902624a8cbdd086be9
Type its first eight characters to confirm: e8196695
Signed by the Head of Complaints on 2026-11-04, a date typed with --today on a machine dated 2026-11-12, fingerprint e8196695. Written to closure/record.md.
```

The fingerprint is one SHA-256 hash over the memo, your rulings, the letter, the plan, every evidence file, the board's approval and the tool's own code. Sign writes your role, the date, the full hash and the release into closure/record.md. Change any of those files later and the page asks for a fresh signature. Entries that internal audit or the closer add afterwards leave it standing. On a real finding, sign refuses `--today` and uses the machine's date.

A signature records a role and proves no identity. The terminal prompt only stops a script from signing by accident, so the financial institution's access controls decide who may run sign.

## Before you sign

Read the whole screen sign prints, then go back over these:

- Every Cleared line, above all any made before you held the role.
- The Not checked line and the count of ties on typed text.
- The misses that `python3 -I finding/finding.py eval <folder>` lists. On MRA-CMP-07 it catches 24 of 27 planted errors, and all three misses are a figure swapped for another on the same page.
- The five points the [Check section](../finding/README.md#check) leaves to a reader, such as figures that disagree between two documents.

An empty list is a floor, because a wrong figure that happens to sit on its cited page still ties. Read each sentence against its page.

To refuse, delete a cleared line or change it from `cleared`, and the row comes back. Or answer the role prompt with anything other than your role, and sign records nothing.

Every case here is invented, and the tool has not yet run on a real finding.

# The finding owner

This page is for the person on the business side who owns a finding, such as the Head of Complaints in the invented case MRA-CMP-07. The tool asks two things of you. You rule on each row the check could not tie, and once nothing is left you sign.

The check is plain code with no AI model in it, so one folder checked as of one date always prints the same page. It looks for each figure, date and quotation in the closure memo on the evidence page its cite names. Whether the fix works is left to you, internal audit and the issuer.

## The page you read

From the root folder of the repository:

```sh
python3 -I finding/finding.py check finding/cases/MRA-CMP-07 --today 2026-11-04
```

The `--today` option fixes the date so your screen matches this one, trimmed where it shows `...`:

```text
Finding MRA-CMP-07, a supervisory finding from the Supervisor dated 2026-01-15. Owner: Head of Complaints. Checked as of 2026-11-04, kit release 0.7.1.
...
Memo check: 13 claims, 7 tie, 3 on the list, 1 cleared.
  Line 8: 1,248 is cited to EV-07 p2, and the page does not hold it; the nearest figures on the page are 1,284 and 2. To rule, name: 1,248 #972adb19
  Line 10: EV-12, which is a draft, holds 4 claims, on lines 10, 15 and 16, that match its pages and wait on a person's signature. To rule, name: EV-12 draft #81b3b231
  Line 16: the sample period for M2 starts 2026-01-05, before the fix took effect on 2026-03-17, so the sample mixes items from before and after the fix. To rule, name: sample period for M2 #106ddd50
  Cleared: line 8, March 2026, by the Head of Complaints on 2026-11-04: The page says January to March, and the plan year is 2026.
  7 ties rest on text a person typed: 7 in plain-text evidence, none on a page typed into a cover.
  Not checked: 1 figure written in words, line 6 (three).
Signature: none yet.
...
Needs a person:
  Head of Complaints: M2, the list (3 rows).
...
```

The Owner field names the role your rulings and signature must carry. The command exits 1 while anyone still has something to do.

## What each row means

Each row opens with the memo line it concerns, and a row you can rule on ends with the words a ruling uses to name it.

- Line 8 says 1,248 and the cited page says 1,284, which looks like two digits swapped in typing. The memo is wrong.
- Line 10 is one row for a draft. The quality review EV-12 supports four claims in the memo, and they wait until someone signs it.
- Line 16 says the tested sample starts before the fix took effect, so it mixes items from both sides of the fix.

Other rows name a missing cite, a cite to a file that is not there, or a page with no text that someone has to type. No ruling clears a row for a memo or plan that calls the finding closed before the closer has recorded it, so someone rewords the line.

Below the rows, each Cleared line gives the role, date and reason of a past ruling. The Not checked line names figures the check skipped, such as a number written in words.

## How to rule

A ruling is one line in closure/rulings.md. It gives the memo line, the name the row prints at its end, the ruling, your role, a date and a reason.

```text
Line 16 | sample period for M2 #106ddd50 | cleared | Head of Complaints | 2026-11-04 | Items from before 2026-03-17 were drawn on purpose as a baseline error rate.
```

A `cleared` ruling takes the row off the list and prints your reason on every later page. To send a row back, rule `fix the memo`, or `fix the evidence` when a document must change or be signed again. That row stays on the list until the fix lands, and your line stays as a record that the check caught it.

The check ignores a ruling from another role, one dated after the check or one with no reason, and says why under the rows. The mark after `#` stands for the claim, its cite and its sentence. Reword the sentence or move the cite and the row returns under a new mark, so you rule again.

The tool accepts `cleared` on any row that offers a name, a wrong figure included, so the restraint is yours. Use it only when you can see the memo is right and why the check missed it, such as a figure the page spells out in words. Send a wrong figure back every time. A colleague or an AI assistant may draft rulings for you to accept. The check cannot tell who typed a line, so every line naming your role counts as yours.

## The fingerprint and the signature

Sign refuses while a row is on the list, a milestone is unsigned or the board has not approved the plan, among other reasons. When no refusal is left, sign shows the full check page first and then asks two questions. Here it runs on a copy of the second invented case:

```sh
cp -R finding/cases/IA-CMP-02 walk-02
python3 -I finding/finding.py sign walk-02 --today 2026-11-04
```

```text
Ready to sign: the folder's fingerprint is e8196695. Internal audit records this as what it tests.

Type the finding owner's role to sign: Head of Complaints
Fingerprint e8196695310808ca7b781c85652770d0806694a69b43af902624a8cbdd086be9
Type its first eight characters to confirm: e8196695
Signed by the Head of Complaints on 2026-11-04, a date typed with --today on a machine dated 2026-11-12, fingerprint e8196695. Written to closure/record.md.
```

The fingerprint is one SHA-256 hash over the memo, your rulings, the letter, the plan, every evidence file, the board's approval and the tool's own code. Sign writes your role, the date, the full hash and the release into closure/record.md. Change any of those files later and the page asks for a fresh signature. Entries that internal audit or the closer add afterwards leave it standing. On a real finding, sign refuses `--today` and uses the machine's date.

A signature records a role and proves no identity. The terminal prompt only stops a script from signing by accident, so the financial institution's access controls decide who may run sign.

## Before you sign

Read the whole screen sign prints, then go back over these:

- Every Cleared line, above all any made before you held the role.
- The Not checked line and the count of ties on typed text.
- The misses that `python3 -I finding/finding.py eval <folder>` lists. On MRA-CMP-07 it catches 24 of 27 planted errors, and all three misses are a figure swapped for another on the same page.
- The five points the [Check section](../finding/README.md#check) leaves to a reader, such as figures that disagree between two documents.

An empty list is a floor, because a wrong figure that happens to sit on its cited page still ties. Read each sentence against its page.

To refuse, delete a cleared line or change it from `cleared`, and the row comes back. Or answer the role prompt with anything other than your role, and sign records nothing.

Every case here is invented, and the tool has not yet run on a real finding.

# finding: the walk

Run every command from the kit root, the folder that holds finding/. On Windows, type `py -I finding\finding.py` wherever this page says `finding/finding`, and do the copies and edits in File Explorer and a text editor. The walk uses `--today 2026-11-04` so your screen matches this page.

## 1. The line that opens every screen

Every check, and every refusal about a finding, starts with this line:

```
This folder may hold confidential supervisory information. Keep it on a machine the institution has approved, and share nothing from it outside the institution.
```

`finding/finding new ../findings/DEMO-01` run a second time prints only its refusal, `Refused: ../findings/DEMO-01 already exists.`, because it has read no finding, and so does `new` on a path inside the kit. The tool sends nothing anywhere. Keeping the folder on an approved machine is up to the people using it.

## 2. Open a finding

```
finding/finding new ../findings/DEMO-01
```

It prints `Made ../findings/DEMO-01. Fill the header lines in finding.md and paste each part of the letter under its heading, then fill plan.md.` and makes `DEMO-01/` in a findings folder beside the kit, with finding.md, plan.md, an empty evidence/, and closure/ with its memo, record, rulings and measures templates. No template holds a SYNTHETIC line to delete. The last part of the path is the finding's id. A folder inside the kit is refused, so `finding/finding new DEMO-01` from the kit root prints `Refused: DEMO-01 is inside the kit's own folders. Make the finding folder outside the kit, such as ../findings/DEMO-01 from the kit root.` To see what to fill first, check the empty folder:

```
finding/finding check ../findings/DEMO-01
```

It prints the opening line, then `Not ready: finding.md has no Institution yet. Fill that line, then check again.` and exits 1, because the header lines are empty. Remove the folder when you have seen enough:

```
rm -r ../findings/DEMO-01
```

## 2b. From a letter to a first check

A real letter has no such headings, so a person fills the header lines and puts each passage under the heading it answers. Here is a short invented letter in that shape, with one milestone:

```
finding/finding new ../findings/DEMO-02
cat > ../findings/DEMO-02/finding.md <<'END'
# Finding DEMO-02
Identifier: DEMO-02
Institution: Harbour Example Bank
Issuer: the Supervisor
Letter date: 2026-09-14
Kind of matter: supervisory finding
Owner role: Head of Complaints

## Concern
Complaint files are not kept for the full period.

## Cause
No procedure sets the retention period.

## Consequence
Files the Supervisor asked for could not be found.

## Corrective action
Set the period in a procedure and move the files.

## Commitment
Report progress to the Supervisor within 60 days.
END
echo '| M1 Issue the retention procedure | Head of Complaints | 2027-01-31 | The procedure sets the period | EV-01 | A sample of files meets the period |' >> ../findings/DEMO-02/plan.md
finding/finding check ../findings/DEMO-02 --today 2026-11-04
```

It prints the full screen, opening with this and ending with what needs a person:

```
Finding DEMO-02, a supervisory finding from the Supervisor dated 2026-09-14. Owner: Head of Complaints. Checked as of 2026-11-04, kit release 0.7.1.

Milestones
M1 Issue the retention procedure. Head of Complaints, committed 2027-01-31 proposed. Not started.
```

That first full check fixes the letter's text. Change a word and check again:

```
sed 's/for the full period/for the whole period/' ../findings/DEMO-02/finding.md > ../findings/DEMO-02/finding.new
mv ../findings/DEMO-02/finding.new ../findings/DEMO-02/finding.md
finding/finding check ../findings/DEMO-02 --today 2026-11-04
```

```
Refused: the Concern in finding.md is not the text first checked on 2026-11-04. The Supervisor's words do not change; restore them, or run check --repaste if the first paste was wrong.
```

If the first paste was wrong, `finding/finding check ../findings/DEMO-02 --repaste --today 2026-11-04` records the correction and keeps the evidence record, the deny list and any signature. Every later page says the text was corrected and on what date, and the folder's log holds the line.

The first check also puts the financial institution's name and any run of two or three capitalised words from the letter on the deny list, and a page that would print one is refused. A run that holds a role word or a document word, such as Head or Procedure, is a title and stays off the list, so an institution's file named for a procedure the letter cites keeps its name. If a term on the list is an ordinary word or a title, the refusal says to add it to `role-words.txt` beside finding.md, and the next check clears it. That holds when the term sits in the name of one of the institution's files too, because renaming the file breaks its link to the institution's records. A word of the institution's name clears the same way, and the page then counts it. The institution's full name never clears, so its refusal does not offer the file. `finding/finding check ../findings/DEMO-02 --names` prints the list, for the person who asks. Every other page prints only its count. Remove the folder:

```
rm -r ../findings/DEMO-02
```

## 3. Read the invented finding

```
finding/finding check finding/cases/MRA-CMP-07 --today 2026-11-04
```

It prints this screen and exits 1:

```
This folder may hold confidential supervisory information. Keep it on a machine the institution has approved, and share nothing from it outside the institution.

Finding MRA-CMP-07, a supervisory finding from the Supervisor dated 2026-01-15. Owner: Head of Complaints. Checked as of 2026-11-04, kit release 0.7.1.

Milestones
M1 Approve revised complaint taxonomy. Head of Complaints, committed 2026-02-28. Present and signed on 2026-02-20.
M2 Reissue intake procedure. Head of Complaints, committed 2026-03-15. Present, unsigned: EV-08 was revised on 2026-04-02, after its signature of 2026-03-14. SLIPPED by 234 days.
M3 Quality review of reclassified complaints. Complaints QA lead, committed 2026-04-30. Present, unsigned: EV-12 is a draft. SLIPPED by 188 days.
M4 Extend taxonomy to the mobile app chat channel. Head of Digital, committed 2026-06-30. Not started. SLIPPED by 127 days.

Board summary, a draft for the finding owner
Flagged commitments: M2 slipped 234 days, M3 slipped 188 days, M4 slipped 127 days.
Quarterly progress:
  Quarter ending 2026-03-31: 2 milestones due, 1 signed, 1 below signed.
  Quarter ending 2026-06-30: 4 milestones due, 1 signed, 3 below signed.
Plan approval: board minutes E-PLAN-1, signed by the Company Secretary on 2026-02-10.

Commitment table, the institution's response in the Supervisor's five-part form, from plan.md
Concern, Cause and Consequence: as written in finding.md.
Corrective action:
| Milestone | Owner role | Committed date |
| M1 Approve revised complaint taxonomy | Head of Complaints | 2026-02-28 |
| M2 Reissue intake procedure | Head of Complaints | 2026-03-15 |
| M3 Quality review of reclassified complaints | Complaints QA lead | 2026-04-30 |
| M4 Extend taxonomy to the mobile app chat channel | Head of Digital | 2026-06-30 |
Commitment: full remediation by 2026-06-30.

Closure memo: present, not tested by internal audit yet.
Internal audit: none recorded.
Supervisor closure: none recorded.
Board approval: none recorded.
Memo check: 13 claims, 7 tie, 3 on the list, 1 cleared.
  Line 8: 1,248 is cited to EV-07 p2, and the page does not hold it; the nearest figures on the page are 1,284 and 2. To rule, name: 1,248 #972adb19
  Line 10: EV-12, which is a draft, holds 4 claims, on lines 10, 15 and 16, that match its pages and wait on a person's signature. To rule, name: EV-12 draft #81b3b231
  Line 16: the sample period for M2 starts 2026-01-05, before the fix took effect on 2026-03-17, so the sample mixes items from before and after the fix. To rule, name: sample period for M2 #106ddd50
  Cleared: line 8, March 2026, by the Head of Complaints on 2026-11-04: The page says January to March, and the plan year is 2026.
  7 ties rest on text a person typed: 7 in plain-text evidence, none on a page typed into a cover.
  Not checked: 1 figure written in words, line 6 (three).
Signature: none yet.
Deny list: 3 names.

Needs a person:
  Head of Complaints: M2, the list (3 rows).
  Complaints QA lead: M3.
  Head of Digital: M4.
  Internal audit: its reference in closure/record.md.
  The Supervisor: its closure notice.

Under Milestones, M1 is present and signed. M2 lists two files in plan.md, EV-07 the intake procedure and EV-08 the register of staff trained on it. EV-07 is signed, but EV-08 was revised after its signature, so M2 is unsigned. M3 is unsigned because its quality review is still a draft, and M4 has no evidence at all. All three are SLIPPED. The board summary counts each quarter's due and signed milestones and names the board minutes that approved the plan. The commitment table is the institution's response in the Supervisor's five-part form. The closure lines show a draft memo that internal audit has not tested, no closure record and no board approval yet. The memo check and its list come in step 7. The deny list line counts the names the check keeps off every page, and the last block names what needs a person, grouped by who.

## 4. Change a signed file

Steps 4 and 5 work on a copy, so the shipped case stays as it is. Copy the case, keep a copy of EV-03, the signed taxonomy, change one word of its body, and check again:

```
cp -R finding/cases/MRA-CMP-07 walk-07
cp walk-07/evidence/EV-03-complaint-taxonomy.md walk-07/EV-03.keep
sed 's/with three subcategories/with four subcategories/' walk-07/EV-03.keep > walk-07/evidence/EV-03-complaint-taxonomy.md
finding/finding check walk-07 --today 2026-11-04
```

M1 moves back and joins the flagged commitments:

```
M1 Approve revised complaint taxonomy. Head of Complaints, committed 2026-02-28. Present, unsigned: EV-03 changed since it was signed. SLIPPED by 249 days.
```

```
Flagged commitments: M1 slipped 249 days, M2 slipped 234 days, M3 slipped 188 days, M4 slipped 127 days.
```

The quarterly counts drop to 0 signed, and M1 joins what the Head of Complaints has to do. Put the signed text back and check again:

```
mv walk-07/EV-03.keep walk-07/evidence/EV-03-complaint-taxonomy.md
finding/finding check walk-07 --today 2026-11-04
```

The screen matches step 3 again, and M1 reads `Present and signed on 2026-02-20`. The state file, `.finding-state.json`, kept the hash EV-03 had when it was signed, because the check never records a changed file over a signed one with the same signature date. Plain `ls` hides that file, and `cp -R folder/* copy` leaves it behind, so copy a whole folder with `cp -R folder copy` as this step does. With the state file gone, the page names what was signed before the new first check, because a change before then cannot be seen.

## 5. Call the finding closed

A line that says the finding itself is closed goes on the list until the closer's entry is in the record, and no ruling clears it. Any other use of the word closed, such as accounts closed in error, goes on the list for the owner to rule on. A use with the two words before it and the two after as finding.md has them, as when a plan copies the letter's own wording, is no row.

```
echo "The finding is closed." >> walk-07/plan.md
finding/finding check walk-07 --today 2026-11-04
```

The page prints in full, and the list grows to 4 rows with this one:

```
  Line 10: closed in plan.md claims the finding is closed, and only the Supervisor closes a supervisory finding. Reword the line, as no ruling clears this row.
```

Remove the copy:

```
rm -r walk-07
```

## 6. A finding that waits only on people

```
finding/finding check finding/cases/IA-CMP-02 --today 2026-11-04
echo $?
```

This internal audit finding has both milestones signed, board minutes that approve the plan, and the board's approval of closure. Internal audit has entered nothing yet, because the owner signs first. The screen says `Supervisor closure: not applicable to an internal audit finding.` and ends with these lines:

```
Memo check: 13 claims, 13 tie, 0 on the list.
  13 ties rest on text a person typed: 13 in plain-text evidence, none on a page typed into a cover.
  Not checked: 2 figures written in words, line 6 (five) and line 8 (five).
Signature: none yet.
Deny list: 3 names.

Needs a person:
  Head of Complaints: the signature, which comes first.
  Internal audit: its reference in closure/record.md.
Ready to sign: the folder's fingerprint is e8196695. Internal audit records this as what it tests.
```

The exit code is 1, because the owner has not signed. The invented evidence is plain text, so every tie counts as resting on typed text, and none sits on a page typed into a cover, so none needs a second person's Checked by line. The two figures written in words are left for a reader. The fingerprint changes with any release that changes the tool's code, and the Finding line names the release, so your screen matches this page only on release 0.7.1.

## 7. The list

Step 3 ended with the memo check for MRA-CMP-07. The check read every figure and date written in digits and every quotation in closure/memo.md and looked for each one on the evidence page its cite names:

```
Memo check: 13 claims, 7 tie, 3 on the list, 1 cleared.
  Line 8: 1,248 is cited to EV-07 p2, and the page does not hold it; the nearest figures on the page are 1,284 and 2. To rule, name: 1,248 #972adb19
  Line 10: EV-12, which is a draft, holds 4 claims, on lines 10, 15 and 16, that match its pages and wait on a person's signature. To rule, name: EV-12 draft #81b3b231

  Cleared: line 8, March 2026, by the Head of Complaints on 2026-11-04: The page says January to March, and the plan year is 2026.
  7 ties rest on text a person typed: 7 in plain-text evidence, none on a page typed into a cover.
  Not checked: 1 figure written in words, line 6 (three).
```

The memo says 1,248 where the procedure says 1,284. The figure 31 and the three dates on the Fix effective and Sample period lines come from a quality review that is still a draft, so EV-12 gets one row for the 4 claims that match its pages until a person signs it. The sample for the tested control also starts before its fix. That sample row is not a claim, so the 13 claims are the 7 that tie, the 1,248, the 4 on the EV-12 row and the 1 cleared. Each row ends with what a ruling names to clear it. The finding owner has already cleared one row in closure/rulings.md, and the page prints it with its reason. Move that file aside on a copy to see it come back:

```
cp -R finding/cases/MRA-CMP-07 walk-07
mv walk-07/closure/rulings.md walk-07/rulings.keep
finding/finding check walk-07 --today 2026-11-04
```

With the rulings moved aside, the row for March 2026 comes back, because EV-07 page 2 holds no date:

```
Memo check: 13 claims, 7 tie, 4 on the list.
